Package com.acxiom.emailaudit.reporting

Class BusinessCategoryMapper

java.lang.Object
com.acxiom.emailaudit.reporting.BusinessCategoryMapper
public final class BusinessCategoryMapper extends Object
Maps technical audit rule IDs to business-friendly category names.

This is a pure lookup — no finding analysis, no severity logic, no business wording beyond the category label itself. One responsibility: rule ID → category name.

What changed and why

  • BROKEN_ANCHOR was mapped to "Legal — Unsubscribe Link". That rule validates in-page fragment links (e.g. href="#section" resolving to a matching id on the page) — it has nothing to do with unsubscribe compliance. A finding like "Jump to membership details → #membership-details does not exist" showing up under a "Legal — Unsubscribe Link" category is actively misleading. Now mapped to "Inventory & Inspect Links", alongside LINK_VALIDATION — both are link-integrity checks.
  • LINK_TEXT_VALIDATION was mapped to "Tracking Links & CTAs". That rule flags generic anchor text (e.g. "click here"); it isn't a CTA or tracking-parameter check. Moved to "Inventory & Inspect Links" for the same reason as above.
  • Both moves also bring the Excel category scheme in line with ReportSectionMapper, which already groups both of these rule IDs under ReportSection.LINKS for the dashboard — so the two reports no longer disagree on where these findings belong.

Stateless and thread-safe.
